newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt telecoms bill goes before Senate.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt telecoms bill goes before Senate.

text.p: The Italian government on Monday presented to the Senate public works commission an amendment to Post Minister Antonio Maccanico's draft bill to set up a telecoms sector watchdog authority and establish antitrust rules in television broadcasting.
The amendment concerns the part of the draft bill that covers the authority's allocation of broadcasting frequencies by January 31, 1998, and the issue of new licences by April 30, 1998.
The authority will have to set time limits by which broadcasters who exceed antitrust limits have to conform to the rules by moving channels to satellite or cable.
The authority also has to decide when state broadcaster RAI must transform one of its three channels into one which does not use commercial advertising.
The Constitutional Court ruled three years ago that no single proprietor should be allowed to keep three TV channels, but the government extended current ownership rules last year.
Opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi's Mediaset company has three national terrestrial channels, as has RAI.
Media sources say it is likely one of Berlusconi's channels will have to be transferred to satellite, and one of RAI's channels will become a regionalised, local broadcaster.

The authority's decision, for which a date has not been fixed, should take account of "the actual development of radio and television programmes by satellite and cable," according to the text of the government's amendment.

When the law is passed the authority will be able to allocate frequencies to broadcasting concession holders which have national coverage of less than 90 percent, excluding those transmitting by coded signals.

With the presentation of this amendment, the government hopes to speed up the creation of the telecoms sector authority -- delayed by opposition from the hard-left Communist Refoundation and Berlusconi's centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance -- which is also a necessary precondition for the planned privatisation of state telecoms holding Stet.
